issues.failure_explanation: The example's diffusion matrix σ diag(x^1,...,x^d) is not uniformly elliptic on all of R^d because it degenerates whenever any coordinate is zero. Also b(s,x)=r x and σ(s,x)=σ diag(x) are unbounded on R^d, so they are not C^1_b as required by Assumption assumptionpde. Thus the claim that the assumptions hold is false without restricting the state space.

failure_location.quote: Then, it is straightforward to check that Assumptions~\ref{assumptions} and \ref{assumptionpde} hold.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the state space to a domain where σ is uniformly elliptic and b,σ are bounded, or modify Assumption assumptionpde to allow local ellipticity and unbounded coefficients with appropriate localization.
issues.overall_effect: The financial example and the numerical experiments based on Black-Scholes are not covered by the stated theoretical assumptions. The claimed applicability to this model is not justified without a domain restriction or modified assumptions.
issues.title: Example falsely claims Black-Scholes model satisfies global PDE assumptions
issues.why_classification: The defect is in an illustrative example rather than a main theorem, but it falsely claims the main assumptions are satisfied for the primary financial application. A contained modification of the example or assumptions can repair it without changing the main theoretical results.

issues.failure_explanation: For p>2, the term ∫ E|Z_s|^p ds cannot be bounded by (1/N)||Z||^p_{H^p}. By Hölder, the correct factor is (1/N)^{1-p/2}, which grows with N for p>2. Hence the absorption argument using N>2C_2 fails for p>2. The proposition is only justified as written for p=2.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either restrict the proposition to p=2 or supply a correct S^p×H^p a priori estimate for p>2, e.g. via standard BSDE estimates using a different splitting.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed p≥2 estimate in Proposition xyzbound is unsupported for p>2. Downstream results use only the p=2 case, so they are not invalidated by this particular defect.
issues.title: Proposition xyzbound proof invalid for p>2
issues.why_classification: The defect is a proof gap in the p>2 part of an auxiliary estimate. A standard alternative proof or a restriction to p=2 fixes it without affecting the main results.

issues.failure_explanation: Combining the terminal error bound E|δY_T|^2 ≤ C Δt with the first inequality gives ≤ C(Δt + λ^2 Δt). To conclude ≤ C λ^2 Δt, one needs λ≥1 (or λ bounded below by a positive constant). The theorem only assumes λ>2K_y, which allows λ<1 when K_y=0. For small λ the bound is false because the error does not vanish as λ→0.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the condition λ≥1 (or λ≥C for a suitable constant) to Theorem discerror and to corollaries that invoke this second inequality, or retain the Δt term in the bound.
issues.overall_effect: The second inequality in Theorem discerror is not valid for small λ. The main asymptotic results, which use λ≈Δt^{-1/2} and thus large λ for small Δt, are unaffected.
issues.title: Theorem discerror second inequality requires λ≥1 but only assumes λ>2K_y
issues.why_classification: The repair is a simple additional parameter condition. The regime of interest has λ→∞, so the main results and rates survive.

issues.failure_explanation: The Z term on the right-hand side of the Young inequality receives coefficient 3(1+1/(16K_z^2 Δt))·2K_z^2 Δt = 6K_z^2 Δt + 3/8. To move it to the left-hand side and leave at least 1/2, one needs 1 − (6K_z^2 Δt + 3/8) ≥ 1/2, i.e. Δt ≤ 1/(48K_z^2). The stated condition Δt<1/(16K_z^2) is insufficient.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the condition with Δt<1/(48K_z^2) or adjust the Young's inequality constants so that 1/(16K_z^2) suffices.
issues.overall_effect: The absorption step in the proof of Theorem discerror is not justified under the stated condition. The theorem may still be true with a smaller Δt, but the condition as written needs correction.
issues.title: Theorem discerror Δt condition insufficient for the claimed Z-term absorption
issues.why_classification: A simple constant in a technical condition needs adjustment; the method and rates are unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: The integral term ∫ E|Y_s−Y_ti| ds is not bounded by Δt^{3/2} per interval in general. It is only bounded by O(Δt)+O(Δt sqrt(∫E|Z|^2)) per interval, and its sum over intervals is O(Δt^{1/2}) using Corollary apbcor. The proof drops this term without justification.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a Cauchy–Schwarz argument to bound the sum of the omitted term by O(Δt^{1/2}) using Corollary apbcor, or include the term explicitly in the bound.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Theorem better is incomplete as written. The final bound may still hold because the omitted sum is O(Δt^{1/2}), which is already present in the bound, but the derivation needs an additional argument. Corollary cor:final, which relies on Theorem better, is consequently not fully supported as written.
issues.title: Theorem better proof drops an unaccounted integral term
issues.why_classification: The missing step is a standard local estimate that does not change the final rate or require new proof architecture.
